title: Senior Director, Product Management
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. About the Role Veeam is looking for a Senior Director, Product Management to own product strategy, roadmap, and execution for our Data and AI Security portfolio, including Data Security and AI Security Posture Management (AISPM). This portfolio came into Veeam through the Securiti AI acquisition and is a strategic priority area as Veeam builds out data and AI trust capabilities.   This person reports directly to the President of Products and Technology and acts as the connective tissue between market opportunity, engineering execution, and executive strategy. They will set direction for the data security /AISPM product team, represent product strategy in executive-level conversations, and be accountable for translating strategy into a roadmap the broader org can rally behind.   This is a high-visibility, high-autonomy role, looking for someone who can move fast and make sound calls independently.   What You’ll Do Responsible for the Data and AI Security portfolio and adjacent data access governance capabilities   Lead and develop the product management team supporting this portfolio, setting clear goals and raising the bar on execution   Translate company strategy into a prioritized roadmap, balancing customer needs, technical feasibility, and business impact across a recently acquired product line   Represent product strategy directly to the President of Products and Technology and executive team, with clear, data-driven narratives   Partner cross-functionally with Engineering, Design, Marketing, and Sales leadership to ensure alignment from concept to launch   Own pricing, packaging, and go-to-market input for the data and AI security product line   Bring a strong point of view on the data security posture management and AI governance competitive landscape, and use that to inform roadmap decisions What You’ll Bring 12+ years in product management, with meaningful time leading product teams   Direct experience in data security, data access governance, cloud security posture management (CSPM/CIEM), or AI governance/security   Data loss prevention (DLP) experience   Track record owning product strategy for a security or data governance platform, ideally in a company that scaled or was acquired   Proven ability to operate with high autonomy and report directly to executive leadership, including comfort presenting to executive team with minimal hand-holding   Strong analytical skills; comfortable making prioritization calls using data plus judgment when data is incomplete   Exceptional written and verbal communication; can distill complexity into a clear, executive-ready narrative   Demonstrated success driving cross-functional alignment across Engineering, Design, Sales, and Marketing   Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent practical experience Bonus Skills Experience integrating an acquired product line into a larger platform   Experience with platform and integrations product management (RBAC, MFA, API-level access controls)   Mix of startup and enterprise experience   #LI-SO2   What you'll get Unlimited paid time off, 12 paid holidays including 4 global VeeaMe Days for self-care and 24 paid volunteer hours annually through Veeam Cares Paid parental leave: 8 weeks for all parents, 16 weeks for birthing parents Medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on your first day Mental health support, therapy sessions, and digital wellness tools via our Employee Assistance Program 401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions Fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support through Maven, plus paid volunteer time AirVet: 24/7 virtual veterinary care at no cost Legal services, identity protection, and supplemental health insurance options Tax-advantaged spending accounts for healthcare, dependent care, and commuting Opportunities to learn and grow through on-demand libraries (LinkedIn Learning, O’Reilly), mentoring, workshops, and learning events like our annual Global Day of Learning Pay Transparency Veeam is committed to pay transparency and equitable compensation.

title: Data Governance & Data Catalog Lead
description: Job Family : Data Science Consulting Travel Required : Up to 10% Clearance Required : Ability to Obtain Public Trust What You Will Do : Lead governance workstreams and small delivery teams to design and implement data/AI governance programs that are actionable and sustainable. Own client relationships for your workstream by setting expectations, facilitating executive discussions, and driving alignment across business, IT, privacy, security, and legal stakeholders. Advise, present solution and governance alternatives analysis, implement, and operate new Collibra Data Catalog instance. Perform hands-on Collibra Data Catalog implementation support, to include leading prioritization of high-value features and work management scoping. Design and operationalize governance operating models including council structures, data stewardship models, decision escalation paths, and integrated controls across data, analytics, and AI. Define implementation roadmaps that connect strategy to execution, including sequencing, dependency management, change management, and measurable adoption outcomes. Establish AI governance and responsible AI guardrails such as model and use case inventory, risk management workflow, review boards, documentation standards, third-party oversight, and ongoing compliance reporting. Institute tactical and functional data governance operations and controls that assist in operationalizing program and product-level governance. Translate governance needs into scalable enablement including templates, playbooks, training, and communications that improve adoption and reduce operational friction. Contribute to growth and pursuits by supporting proposal development, scoping, staffing plans, and the creation of reusable assets and accelerators. Ability to travel as needed based on client and project needs What You Will Need : Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DoD “PUBLIC TRUST”. Bachelor’s degree obtained. SEVEN (7) or more years of relevant experience with progressive responsibility, including workstream leadership and oversight of junior staff. Experience leading client workstreams end-to-end, including planning, facilitation, issue resolution, and executive communications. Experience to configure, architect, advise, and perform hands-on implementation of Collibra Data Catalog platform. Experience shaping roadmaps and operating models that connect governance to delivery, adoption, and measurable outcomes. Experience delivering consulting or client-facing work, including workshops, written deliverables, and stakeholder management. Experience with AI governance concepts such as model risk considerations, transparency and documentation, monitoring, and responsible AI practices. Ability to travel as needed based on client and project needs What Would Be Nice To Have : Experience supporting governance programs in public sector, transportation, and/or other regulated environments. Demonstrated knowledge of data governance fundamentals, such as data stewardship, data lifecycle, metadata, data quality, privacy, and access controls. Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex topics in clear, practical language and produce polished client-ready outputs. Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and deliver high-quality work products in a fast-paced environment. Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (Information Systems, Public Policy, Business, Data/Computer Science, Engineering, or similar). Hands-on experience with additional governance and privacy tooling such as Microsoft Purview, Alation, Informatica, OneTrust, Immuta, Datadog, or similar platforms. Experience connecting Collibra with other platforms, to include Databricks (Unity Catalog), and onboarding new data assets to the data catalog and metadata ecosystem. Experience designing or facilitating AI literacy, adoption, and change management efforts, including training plans and communications. Familiarity with modern data platforms and delivery patterns such as Azure, Databricks, Snowflake, lakehouse architectures, and data products. Certifications in areas pertaining to data governance, privacy, security, cloud, or analytics. The annual salary range for this position is $113,000.00-$188,000.00. Compensation decisions depend on a wide range of factors, including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, security clearances, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. What We Offer : Guidehouse offers a comprehensive, total rewards package that includes competitive compensation and a flexible benefits package that reflects our commitment to creating a diverse and supportive workplace. title: SPAR Research Manager
description: Help SPAR’s mentors become excellent research leads. We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis. About Kairos Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs: SPAR : The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others. Generator Residency : In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more. Global Challenges Project : A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley. Pathfinder Fellowship : Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work. We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem. The Role SPAR is a remote, part-time fellowship that runs twice a year, with 800+ mentees, 250+ mentors, and 6,000+ applicants in the latest cohort. Many of our mentors are early-career researchers leading a team for the first time, and the quality of their mentorship shapes what hundreds of mentees learn and produce each round. We’re looking for a Research Manager to be a mentor to our mentors. You’ll work with the researchers leading SPAR projects, helping them run their teams well, handle difficult situations, and get their work in front of the right audiences. You’ll work closely with SPAR’s program lead, and there’s room to take on broader ownership of how SPAR supports its mentors. What You’ll Do Support mentors across the round. You’ll be the main point of contact for a portfolio of mentors. You’ll check in with them regularly and help them scope projects, set expectations with mentees, and keep their teams on track. Help first-time mentors become strong research leads. Many SPAR mentors are leading a team for the first time. You’ll coach them on running effective meetings, giving feedback, and managing mentees with very different levels of experience. Handle sensitive team situations. When a team runs into conflict, a mentee stops showing up, or a mentor relationship breaks down, you’ll step in, work out what’s going on, and help everyone find a way forward. Advise on research outputs. You’ll help mentors and their teams decide where and how to share their work, including which publications, workshops, and conference venues suit their results. Help shape how SPAR works with mentors. You’ll contribute to how we recruit, onboard, and support mentors, and help raise the bar on research quality across the program as SPAR grows. What you won’t do. With 250+ mentors and 800+ mentees per round, you won’t supervise individual projects in depth or co-author the research. Your impact comes from making mentors better at leading their teams, so more of their projects succeed. Who You Are Solid research experience. You’ve done substantial research yourself, such as a PhD, a research role, or several completed projects. You understand how research projects go well and badly, and mentors take your advice seriously. Strong interpersonal judgment. You handle delicate conversations with tact, and people come to you when things are going wrong. A clear communicator. You write and speak clearly, and you can give direct feedback in a way people can act on. Organized. You’ll support many mentors at once during the round, often against hard deadlines. You keep careful track of commitments and follow through on them. AI safety context. You’re familiar with the AI safety ecosystem and its major research agendas, and you can engage with mentors doing both technical and policy research. You don’t need to be an expert on every agenda. Mission-aligned. You care about how AI development plays out, and you see SPAR as one of the most promising ways to grow the next generation of AI safety researchers. While not required, we especially value: Experience mentoring or managing junior researchers, whether in a lab, an academic group, or a research fellowship like SPAR Publications at ML conferences or in AI policy venues Research experience in AI safety or AI governance Why Work With Us You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. SPAR shapes who becomes an AI safety researcher and how well they learn to do research. SPAR already has a strong brand, a robust mentor and mentee pipeline, and working relationships with most of the top AI safety orgs. We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact. What We Offer Salary : $105,000–$145,000 (baseline), $130,000–$180,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $145,000–$200,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates Location : This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses. Benefits : Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture. Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered. Logistics Start date : Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston. We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1). Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however. Our Culture We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem. We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard. Application Process We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis. Application form (10–20 mins) Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid) Interview (45 mins) Reference checks Work trial (3 days, paid) Offer If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for. This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply. AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more → Questions? Reach out at Know someone who might be a good fit? If your referral gets hired and completes two months with us, we’ll pay you a $10,000 referral bonus. Learn more here . Compensation: $105K – $200K • Multiple Ranges Most locations (baseline) • $105K – $145K London, DC, Boston, NYC • $130K – $180K San Francisco Bay Area • $145K – $200K Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow
